News.title: Imperious Foden back to his best as City refuse to throw in the towel
News.content:
“The aim is to keep pushing and keep them [Arsenal] on their toes,” Foden said. “We’ve seen a lot of things can happen on the final day. I’ve experienced it many times when the game doesn’t go your way. We just have to keep pushing and doing our part.”

Palace faded away after their bright start and will have to play better than this to trouble Arsenal on the final day at Selhurst Park, although they will also have an eye on their Europa Conference League final against Rayo Vallecano the following Wednesday. So the odds remain stacked against City but it is not done yet.

There were six changes to the team that beat Brentford on Saturday, with Erling Haaland, Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki all on the bench, and five of those picked had just 20 starts between them since the turn of the year. Josko Gvardiol was making his first appearance for four months after injury.

On the pitch, though, City’s stand-ins approached things like there was everything still to play for – the title, a place in Saturday’s FA Cup final team and, in some cases, perhaps even their own futures.

After a dicey start, when Palace almost caught the home side cold on a couple of occasions, City gradually found their stride. And no one more so than Foden.

It has been another difficult season for the 2024 PFA Player of the Year but there were glimpses of a corner slowly being turned against Everton and Brentford and he turned it up another notch altogether against Palace.

They say class is permanent and form is temporary and it was no better illustrated in that moment in the 32nd minute when Foden produced one of the assists of the season.

A split second before receiving Matheus Nunes’s pass in a half space a few yards outside the penalty area, Foden glanced briefly over his shoulder.

Then the ball rolled in and the midfielder, knowing exactly where Antoine Semenyo was, played a no-look back-heel into the path of the Ghana forward, who had run off Chris Richards. Semenyo’s finish into the far corner was pinpoint. “It is one of those, sometimes it doesn’t come off but sometimes a risk is worth taking and I’m very delighted it came off,” Foden said. Guardiola was purring. “He is unique close to the box,” the manager added.

News.title: No more growth for UK this year, warns US banking giant
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Rachel Reeves faces a £12bn blow to the public finances over the leadership chaos surrounding Sir Keir Starmer, Goldman Sachs has warned.

The Chancellor will see her fiscal headroom – the breathing space she has to balance the nation’s books – reduced after the recent sharp surge in government borrowing costs, according to the Wall Street bank.

Borrowing costs have climbed around the world since the Iran war but the increases in Britain have been exacerbated by pressure on the Prime Minister to resign.

The yield on 10-year, the return the Treasury offers when it borrows from financial markets, surged to the highest level since 2008 on Tuesday. The yield on 30-year gilts hit its highest point since 1998.

Wes Streeting, a potential leadership challenger, will meet the Prime Minister in Downing Street for a showdown over Sir Keir’s plan to rescue the party after dire local election results and almost 100 calls from Labour MPs for him to resign.

James Moberly, an analyst at Goldman Sachs, said: “We find that some political risk premium has recently crept into the gilt market in recent weeks.”

The Wall Street bank expects the Office for Budget Responsibility to lower its growth forecasts for the British economy as higher energy prices also weaken potential economic output, also putting pressure on the public finances.

Taken together, it will wipe out around half of the Chancellor’s £23.6bn budget headroom – a blow of about £12bn.

Goldman Sachs said a new prime minister would increase the uncertainty over whether the Government was committed to reducing borrowing.

Mr Moberly added the possibility of a Labour leadership change “introduces greater uncertainty” around the Chancellor’s efforts to reduce the budget deficit, “given that it brings with it the risk of a shift in the fiscal rules”.

He said: “More broadly, policy choices will remain constrained by the challenging backdrop of rising spending pressures and an already elevated tax burden irrespective of any changes in leadership.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) JP Morgan chief threatens to axe £3bn UK investment if Labour lurches Left | America’s largest bank warns it could review plans for new London skyscraper HQ

2) Labour blamed for delaying 100-million-barrel North Sea oil project | Energy company urges ministers to bring forward date of new tax system

3) Musk’s desire to control OpenAI was ‘hair raising’ | Sam Altman, the boss of the ChatGPT-maker, made the claim in a Californian court

4 ) Crisp bags turn black and white as snack giant runs out of ink | Japanese manufacturer switches to monochrome packaging amid Iran war supply shortages

5) Tony Blair’s daughter-in-law to run £500m government AI fund | Wife of former prime minister’s son appointed to lead investment committee

What happened overnight

Asian stocks fell as markets digested the lack of progress towards Middle East peace and setbacks that rattled the boom in AI technology.

Iran’s chief negotiator said on Tuesday that Washington must accept Tehran’s latest peace plan or face failure, after Donald Trump warned the truce in the Middle East war was on the brink of collapse.

Both sides have refused to make concessions and repeatedly threatened to resume fighting, but neither appears willing to return to all-out war.

Traders are now looking to China, where Mr Trump is due to land on Wednesday, the first visit by a US president in nearly a decade, saying he expected a “long talk” with counterpart Xi Jinping about Iran.

Hong Kong, Shanghai, Taipei, Sydney, Bangkok, Manila and Kuala Lumpur were all down on Wednesday. Jakarta fell nearly 2pc as the rupiah plunged to a record low.

The conflict in the Middle East has sent energy costs spiralling.

Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz - through which one fifth of the world’s oil supplies usually pass - has virtually ground to a halt.

But oil prices cooled during early Asia trade, with the international benchmark Brent crude down 0.6pc to $107 a barrel, while US benchmark West Texas Intermediate fell 0.5pc to $101 a barrel.

US stocks fell on Tuesday after a surprise surge in inflation hammered hopes of Federal Reserve interest rate cuts.

The US benchmark S&P 500 dropped by 0.2pc while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell by 0.7pc.

News.title: Scientists say rat virus is mutating - but no critical changes yet
News.content:
“We see two particular small mutations in two patients… [but] there’s no changes in the behavior of the virus,” Dr Oude Munnink told the Telegraph. “It’s typical of viruses, because they of course evolve and they make mistakes during their replication.”

Once inside a human or animal cell, viruses replicate at speed. During this process, small errors in the genetic code can emerge – over time, they can build up to change how the pathogen behaves. This occurred during the coronavirus pandemic, when new variants like delta and omicron emerged as Sars-Cov-2 tore through millions of people.

But the Andes hantavirus is not Covid-19, Dr Oude Munnink said. Not only is a dramatic genetic leap less likely when tens rather than millions of people are infected, but the virus itself is thought to be more stable.

The latest samples are “reassuringly” similar to sequences from an outbreak in Argentina in 2018-2019, when 34 people were infected and 11 died in a “super-spreading” event, said Dr Damien Tully, an associate professor in bioinformatics at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine.

“Preliminary analyses indicate only a relatively small degree of change,” he said. “At present, there is no clear evidence… of major genetic shifts, unusual evolution, or reassortment.”

Tracking hantavirus in rats

Still, scientists are concerned about the potential genetic progression of the Andes virus in its primary host: the long-tailed pygmy rice rat.

The small rodent is found in parts of Argentina and Chile, mainly in the temperate forests and humid grasslands of the Patagonian-Andean region.

“The main virus evolution is occurring now in a wildlife reservoir,” said Dr Oude Munnink. “It’s important to do studies in this wildlife reservoir to see the distribution and the viral evolution of this virus in [rats]... I think that’s information we are lacking at the moment.”

Hantavirus cases in Argentina have recently surged, and researchers are now investigating whether this is a statistical blip, a reflection of improved diagnostics, or something more ominous.

Earlier this month, the Ministry of Health said there have been 101 cases since June 2025, around twice as many cases as the year before. The virus, which causes a severe lung disease called hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, killed roughly a third of patients.

Some scientists say changes in land use, including deforestation, may have driven rats into closer contact with people and into new regions. The country has also seen a rise in extreme weather – including a major drought and bouts of intense rainfall – that may have pushed the long-tailed pygmy rice rats out of their usual habitats as they search for food.

But genetic changes cannot yet be ruled out, said Dr Oude Munnink. He compared controlling the Andes virus to the Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (Mers), which is endemic in camels across the Gulf. The fatality rate in humans is roughly 35 per cent.

“I think [the hantavirus] is more or less similar to Mers… that’s circulating in the dromedary reservoir. And of course, the more virus is circulating, the higher chances that there will be mutations,” Dr Oude Munnink said.

“There is a concern, always, that there might be sporadic spillovers. But I think that if we have our diagnostics up and running and we detect the virus if it affects humans… at an early time point, that we still might be able to control the further spread.

“But it does highlight that it might be important to really get your diagnostics assays also Argentina up and running,” he said.

That begins with understanding where the virus is circulating in Argentina, how it is behaving and whether it has changed.

As a starting point, researchers are trying to pinpoint the origins of the latest outbreak. At first, a leading hypothesis suggested the Dutch couple who died from Andes virus contracted it while bird watching near a landfill site on the outskirts of Ushuaia – a port where MV Hondius docked, on the southern tip of Argentina.

Yet the long-tailed pygmy rice rat traditionally lives at least 1,000 miles away in Patagonian Andes, as well as north-western Argentina.

Sports.title: The Man Utd job has been Carrick’s for months with no big name rivals in the race – all he had to do was hold his nerve
Sports.content:
RATTLING Arsenal’s cage so quickly made Michael Carrick a contender for the Manchester United job.

And Red Devils chiefs are convinced they are not making the same mistake as they did with previous interim boss Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.





Carrick fits the bill for the Old Trafford powerbrokers.

United’s communications department had some new starters in the new year and they could have hardly got an easier ride amid Carrick’s soporific press conferences.

On-message and better results are two major boxes ticked after 15 months of previous boss Ruben Amorim rocking the boat.

The only minor complaint some at United had was ­Carrick’s initial reluctance to talk up Bruno Fernandes’ Player of the Year chances.

After some gentle nudging, he has relented in recent media engagements.

United are keeping coy on Carrick’s impact until after the protracted announcement that he is staying on beyond this season.

A more intense schedule, with Champions League midweek matches back in the calendar next season, will be a truer gauge of Carrick’s clout.

The length of his contract needs to be sensible. No six-year nonsense, like David Moyes got. No post-Alex Ferguson United manager has made the three-year mark.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Performance-wise, the Red Devils peaked under Carrick at the very start but results were always bound to take precedence in the run-in.

Ahead of Sunday’s final home game against Nottingham Forest, Carrick has won ten and lost just two of his 15 games back in charge.

Carrick’s opening game on January 17, a 2-0 win against Manchester City — courtesy of goals from Bryan Mbeumo and Patrick Dorgu — was rightly regarded as United’s best ­performance since the 2024 FA Cup final against the same opponents.

Commenting on Carrick’s first days in charge, one senior player said: “It was great all week. It just needs to be great for the game as well, otherwise it dissipates. Thankfully it was.”



Ahead of a trip to Prem leaders Arsenal the following week, the same player said: “How good would it be to rattle Arsenal’s cage?”

They did exactly that, with Matheus Cunha’s late stunner securing a memorable 3-2 win in North London.

And on the two occasions they have lost, to Newcastle and Leeds, the Red Devils have followed it up by winning the next games against Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively.

Carrick’s representatives have been at the club’s Carrington training ground complex this week and the Geordie is edging ever closer to getting the job permanently.

Senior United figures have stressed they have not ruled out an alternative appointment, but that is effectively face-saving at this stage.



The emergence of Bournemouth chief Andoni Iraola as a rival candidate in late April was swiftly swatted away by United’s win over Liverpool earlier this month, which secured Champions League qualification.

The speculation that Iraola was being strongly considered is believed to have been prompted by the out-going Cherries manager’s wish for a plum job amid interest from Palace.

Iraola was on United’s radar as a possible Amorim replacement back in August but there was no concrete contact made by the club.

In October, Carrick made his TV debut on Match of the Day, and staff found him so pleasant to deal with they expected him to return.

He ­analysed the club’s third successive win against Brighton and said, “It brought a smile to my face”.



Less than three months later, they hired him to try to bring a smile to their faces.

Despite the 24-day gap between matches in March and April, Old Trafford chiefs had still not held formal discussions with another coach.

By contrast, in 2022, they had settled on Erik ten Hag as their No 1 choice to take over by mid-March.



All the signs have pointed to ­Carrick being appointed for months, and it was a case of him holding his nerve once the season resumed after the March internationals.

Their season restarted with a shock home defeat to rivals Leeds, but a potential crisis proved just a wobble with a 1-0 victory away to Chelsea five days later.

United’s initial preference was to hire an external candidate, yet it was clear for months there was no one suitable.

The situation was nothing like when Jose Mourinho became available in December 2015 when he was sacked by Chelsea.

Mourinho was a compelling choice that United could not ignore after the turgid football under Louis van Gaal.



With Carrick already in the building for four months, United can get ahead of the curve in what should be a busy a summer when clubs in England and abroad will change coaches.

Carrick leaves Carrington at 6pm most days.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A keen golfer, he has not been spotted on his nearby course in Alderley Edge as he has immersed himself completely in his day job.

For United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, and chief executive, Omar Berrada, banking on a man who took Middlesbrough to the Championship play-offs just once in three seasons is a gamble that has paid off.

Sports.title: How Brighton betting genius Tony Bloom took just 12 months and £2.6million to blow Scottish football apart with Hearts
Sports.content:
WHEN Tony Bloom suggested in August that he wanted to see Hearts as Champions of Scotland within a decade, nobody could have imagined he might be out by NINE years.

Yet on Saturday, less than 12 months after investing in the Tynecastle club, betting billionaire and Brighton owner Bloom could witness the end of a 66-year wait for the crown to return to Edinburgh.



And eight days later, he might be celebrating the prospect of all THREE of the clubs in which he has an interest competing in the Champions League next term.

While Hearts fans spent Thursday morning still raging at the 99th-minute VAR penalty which means Celtic can wrest the title from their hands with a win at Parkhead this weekend, they remain masters of their own destiny.

From playing in the “relegation” portion of the split end of the season last term, to within 90 minutes of ending an obsession.



And while Derek McInnes and his players, of course, deserve the credit, there is no arguing over the identity of the real architect.

The club chief who – just like his former employee turned bitter rival, Brentford’s Matthew Benham – has turned data and analysis in player recruitment into the magic, transformational ingredient.

Who stands on the brink, now, of masterminding the overturning of what has pretty much always been the established order in Scotland – and installing the first non-Old Firm champions since Aberdeen and Sir Alex Ferguson in 1985.

For an initial outlay of just £9.86million to take a 29 per cent stake of “non-voting shares” – which nominally saw no change in the control of the club, which remained with the fan-owned Foundation of Hearts.

And then green-lighting a massive summer recruitment drive at a net cost of barely £500,000 – not so much signing players few fans had ever heard of, but from clubs many of them didn’t know existed.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

All of it poised to add up to the biggest upset in modern Scottish football history.

Bloom’s own words when he spoke to the club in August, soon after the deal was formalised, suggest even “The Lizard” – his nickname on the international poker circuit in the early 2000s – did not envisage such a rapid and remarkable set of affairs.

He said: “I thought that Scottish football could do with a change, a change in dynamics, where it’s not a two-horse race every season, or as it has been for the last 15 years, pretty much a one-horse race.

“For too long, when I’m looking as an outsider, it’s Celtic or Rangers – and by and large, it soon becomes a one-horse race and Celtic are dominating.



“That cannot be good. Scottish football deserves better than that. I thought that I could come in and make a difference.”

A difference? You, as it were…betcha!

Bloom’s investment was the culmination of a collaboration that had been instigated early in 2024, when then-chair Ann Budge and director James Anderson travelled down to London to meet him for the first time.

Anderson recalled he was blown away by Bloom’s “enormous enthusiasm” as the Amex chief explained his vision.

Bloom planned to use Jamestown Analytics, the data company which is an offshoot of Bloom’s Starlizard – named after that card-playing label – to transform Hearts, just as he had rebuilt Brighton and helped Union Saint-Gilloise rise to prominence in Belgium.



It was music to Anderson’s ears, with the millionaire philanthropist having already come to the conclusion that “our more traditional recruitment methods were not working”.

Jamestown had been used by the club from soon afterwards, with its number crunchers leading to Steven Naismith’s departure as coach, replaced by Neil Critchley, in October 2024 – although the new man was gone himself after six months.

Bloom, though, not taking a seat on the board himself – mindful of Uefa’s multi-club ownership regulations – did get the power to appoint a key director, with long-term ally and “trusted associate” James Franks his representative.

And from last summer, it was the full Jamestown experience, with new boss McInnes, who arrived from Kilmarnock, fully bought into the new approach.

In came 13 players, few of them household names in their own living room, for a total cost of £2.6m.



Kilmarnock defender Stuart Findlay was the most familiar face but £1.7m Claudio Braga came from Norwegian second tier Aalesunds, keeper Alexander Schwolow from Union Berlin and winger Alexandros Kyziridis arrived on a free transfer from Slovakians Zemplin Michalovce.

Others included Tomas Bent Magnusson from Icelandic side Valur, Sabah Kerjota of Sambenedettese in Italy’s FOURTH tier, winger Pierre Landry Kabore arriving from Estonia’s Narva Trans and Islam Chesnokov of FC Tobol in Kazakhstan, while 21 players left either permanently or on loan.

McInnes explained: “Every player with more than 3,000 minutes has a rating and that’s every league in the world. That shows you how vast it is.



“The way the model works is if we can fill the squad with players of a high rating then they [the club] feel the only natural outcome is success.

“It is always a zoom call followed up with another zoom call. We would always try and sign a player with good English and I want to keep a Scottish culture and identity here.

“I know every player in Scotland but if you look at the ratings then some of them rate more poorly than you’d expect.

“When players come from wherever they need to know how we work every day and what playing for Hearts is like rather than us changing to suit their culture.”

McInnes was smart, too, not throwing them all in at once, allowing the new recruits to acclimatise but building a sense of unity.



Hearts are prepared to dominate against lesser teams but sit and hit on the counter against better-equipped rivals, always looking to utilise their pace out wide, with Kyziridis the out-ball.

It was not until November 23, at Aberdeen, that Hearts suffered their first defeat of the season, having already recorded wins over both Rangers and Celtic, with further victories over the Old Firm following before Christmas.

Braga, with 14 goals alongside 15-goal top scorer Lawrence Shankland, has been a key player, with Schwolow, Findlay, Kyziridis, Magnusson and midfielder Oisin McEntee, a free transfer from Walsall, regulars – although the latter two are now out injured.

After 43 matches and just five defeats all season, now it comes down to 90 minutes.

Older Jambos will recall, with a shudder, the last time they were in this position.



In 1986, unbeaten in 27 league matches, they needed just a draw at Dundee on the final day to win the title, just six minutes away from a point before substitute Albert Kidd scored twice to allow Celtic to steal their crown.

This time, though, it feels like the beginning of something. Hearts are Blooming.

Sports.title: Southampton push on through Spygate and unveil plans to sell tickets for Championship playoff final despite axe threat
Sports.content:
SOUTHAMPTON have announced ticket information for the Championship play-off final – despite the ongoing “Spygate” drama.

The EFL released a statement on Thursday to confirm that a hearing into the alleged spying attempt will take place next Tuesday at the latest.





But with the final currently scheduled for next Saturday, the Saints have started promoting ticket sales.

That is despite the possibility of them being expelled from the richest game in football.

SunSport revealed the shock moment an alleged secret Southampton spy was caught recording Middlesbrough training last Thursday ahead of their semi-final showdown.

The Saints have been hit with an EFL charge for breaching rules, with the governing body now investigating.



Southampton booked a May 23 Wembley showdown with Hull – who beat Millwall 2-0 on aggregate – after Shea Charles’ extra-time goal KO’d Middlesbrough on Tuesday.

However, we revealed that Boro are pushing for them to be BOOTED OUT of the play-offs and their squad remain on standby in case they are reinstated at the hearing.

Kim Hellberg and his players were at their Rockcliffe HQ on Thursday for a debrief. They have been given Friday and the weekend off but SunSport understands they have been instructed to hold off any holiday plans because they will return to training on Monday in case they get the nod to face Hull.

The Tigers’ own preparations for attempting to net a bumper £180million promotion jackpot have also been scuppered amid the shock Spygate saga.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Bosnian boss Sergej Jakirovic and his men still do not know who they will be facing at Wembley – or even when.

And with the club only able to announce ticket details tonight amid the hold-up for the hearing, fans could be left scrambling regarding travel plans for the showpiece.

The EFL statement came after Southampton were forced to DELETE all ticket information on Wednesday after wrongly releasing information for the final.

Saints say the confusion over tickets was due to the fact they were meant to publish details at the same time as fellow finalists Hull.



Hull sporting director Jarde Dublin revealed that they are still preparing to take on Southampton, but the EFL statement casts yet more huge doubts on whether they will be under the arch next weekend.

The statement read: “The Independent Disciplinary Commission hearing will take place on or before Tuesday 19 May. The exact date remains under discussion and is expected to be confirmed shortly.

“The Commission will issue its decision as soon as possible following consideration of the relevant submissions and evidence. As the proceedings are being conducted by an Independent Disciplinary Commission, the EFL does not control the proposed timetable.

“Notwithstanding this, the EFL continues to plan on the basis that the Championship Play-Off Final will take place as scheduled on Saturday 23 May, with the kick-off time confirmed as 4.30pm. Supporters should, however, be aware that the outcome of the disciplinary proceedings may yet result in changes to the fixture.

“The EFL has a number of contingency plans should they be required, which also includes consideration of any appeal process, if required.”



As SunSport exclusively revealed, Southampton boss Tonda Eckert and/or technical director Johannes Spors could face a stadium ban IF found to have ordered the alleged undercover mission.

The hearing will be by an independent disciplinary commission. The EFL, Southampton and Middlesbrough all have a right to appeal the outcome, which could add on even more time.

Once that final conclusion has been reached, the Football Association then has the authority to potentially intervene and launch their own investigation and sanctions.

Should any alleged spying be found to have been instructed by Eckert or Spors, they hold the jurisdiction to potentially be hit with a suspension.



An individual, identified as intern William Salt, was snapped hiding behind a tree using his mobile phone to spy on the Teessiders’ training session before being confronted by Boro staff and scarpering.

Boro also have details of a credit card used by the ‘spy’ at the golf club next to Rockliffe, part of the entire complex owned by Boro chairman Steve Gibson, which could potentially lead to a paper-trail of past alleged missions.

Salt was photographed on the shoulder of Saints boss Eckert while celebrating his Sky Bet Championship manager of the month award in February.

Salt, highly valued by German Eckert, was not pictured with the boss and other backroom staff last Thursday to mark April’s manager of the month – the same day he was alleged to have been in the North East.

He was also not in the March celebratory photo that was released on April 9.



The image will be part of the evidence Middlesbrough provide to the EFL as they seek for their rivals to be hit with the greatest sporting sanction possible.

But they also suspect they have not been the only alleged victims and believe they will be able to present evidence that at least TWO other clubs were spied on by Southampton.

CCTV from said clubs is also being reviewed. One report has also claimed an ex-Southampton staff member is willing to tell-all regarding the practice of ‘spying’ on opponents before matches in a statement.

Gibson has enlisted the services of high-profile sports lawyer Nick De Marco.

In another twist, Wembley is fully booked every weekend until mid-August following the Bank Holiday. In the unlikely event it is postponed, it could potentially lead to the game being rescheduled for a midweek kick off or may have to be played elsewhere.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho destined to fail at fractured Real Madrid.. but Special One guarantees drama and we’ll be glued to screen
Sports.content:
REAL MADRID are in chaos, the dressing room is fractured and half of the squad are at each other’s throats.

So, naturally, president Florentino Perez has decided the cure for this toxic environment is to bring back Jose Mourinho.





If someone asks you the question “How do you put out a fire?”, it’s unlikely you’ll reply: “Pour on some petrol.” But here we are, the Special One is back at the Bernabeu.

Back at the club where it would be easier to compile a list of the people he didn’t fall out with than the ones he did.

Mourinho’s pedigree speaks for itself — and he was the greatest coach in world football for several years during the mid-late 2000s. But that was a long time ago.

It’s now 11 years since Mourinho, the man who would almost guarantee silverware wherever he went, won a domestic title.

And he has either been sacked or pushed towards the exit in five of his last six jobs.

Ever since his second stint at Chelsea ended in disarray during the 2015-16 season, with terrible results and yet more dressing-room unrest, he has struggled to recapture those former glories.

Reports in Spain suggest that Madridistas are completely divided on his return.

He didn’t exactly endear himself to supporters, having spent three years whingeing about LaLiga referees and lavishing praise on Barcelona shortly after his departure.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Club legend Iker Casillas, who Mourinho tried to banish after branding him a ‘mole’ who had leaked stories to the press, has stated publicly he does not want him back.

He was one of a number of stars who got on the wrong side of the Portuguese during his first spell, with Sergio Ramos and Pepe having fiery bust-ups of their own.

There are plenty more where they came from — we even got to watch Mourinho’s relationship with his Spurs squad deteriorate through the medium of Netflix.

Having said all of that… if you stare at the situation long enough and hard enough, you can see there is a sort of twisted logic to his re-hiring.



The softly-softly approach with Madrid’s sulking superstars clearly isn’t working.

They have been out-thought and out-fought by Barcelona — and suffered the ignominy of surrendering the title to their arch rivals after a lifeless defeat in El Clasico last weekend.

In the last month alone there have been several explosive rows involving some of the club’s biggest names.

Of course, the bust-up between Aurelien Tchouameni and Federico Valverde dominated headlines around the sporting world a couple of weeks ago.



But there has also been an alleged training-ground scrap between Antonio Rudiger and Alvaro Carreras, while Kylian Mbappe was recently involved in a heated row with one of outgoing boss Alvaro Arbeloa’s coaching staff.

The fans have turned, the changing room is in a shambles and the players look unmanageable — so maybe the answer is to bring in one of the game’s great authoritarians.

Will it work? Your guess is as good as mine. What we do know is it will be combustible, dramatic — and it won’t last long. Mourinho doesn’t do long.

Most of us will be watching on with a morbid fascination to see how it all pans out.



Real Madrid are loathed and loved in equal measure around the world. They are admired and despised as football’s true superpower.

But paranoia has set in after two disastrous seasons and — as we’ve seen many times over the years — they will do anything to try and get back to the top.

Perez is already singing off the Mourinho hymn sheet, having spent the best part of an hour ranting and raving in a bizarre press conference yesterday.

The club are in crisis, so they have turned to the king of chaos. Whatever happens, they can’t say they weren’t warned.

Don’t forget Phil



IS Phil Foden back?

It would be a huge boost to England heading into the World Cup next month.

He earned a rare start for City in their 3-0 win over Crystal Palace, keeping their faint title hopes alive, and we definitely saw flashes of the old Foden.

There is so much talent in the England squad but it has been worrying that so many of them — Cole Palmer, Bukayo Saka, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers — have struggled for form and fitness.



You can put Foden in that bracket, too.

But if he can rediscover his mojo in the nick of time, it would be an enormous lift for the Three Lions.

Royal blessing

THINGS are looking incredibly exciting for the King and Queen on the racing front.

Charles and Camilla have a very promising young horse called Portcullis running in the last race at York on Friday and he’ll undoubtedly head to Royal Ascot if he wins again.

Let’s hope she wins because a Royal runner at the Derby meeting would be just the shot in the arm ailing Epsom needs.

Sports.title: FA Youth Cup final chaos as podium collapses and Man City stars sent sprawling while celebrating huge win over Man Utd
Sports.content:
CHAOS erupted at the FA Youth Cup final as the podium collapsed following jubilant Manchester City celebrations.

City sprayed the champagne after beating their noisy neighbours Manchester United.





Reigan Heskey, son of former England star Emile, won the game late on to make up for losing the final to Aston Villa last year.

And watched on by the likes of Pep Guardiola and Phil Foden, the potential City stars of tomorrow were all smiles as they lifted the most illustrious cup in English youth football.

However, midway through the celebrations there was a hiccup as the podium in front of the players’ feet fell over.

As it collapsed several City stars were seen tumbling forwards, with some falling to the floor.

It wasn’t enough to dampen their spirits though, as City continued the party after dusting themselves off.

Such was their reward for a hard-earned victory over United.

Floyd Samba’s excellent free-kick put the hosts in front after 40 minutes at the Joie Stadium – the undersold venue after the game was moved from the Etihad.

Godwill Kukonki headed home less than a minute later to equalise for Darren Fletcher‘s young Red Devils.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

For most of the second half neither team could find the decisive opening to give them the advantage.

But then in the 87th minute, Heskey was on hand to power home the winner.

And Guardiola will doubtless be hoping the City first-team can replicate the youth team’s success against Chelsea at Wembley on Saturday.

He was likely also casting an eye on some future prospects he might fancy for the first team – although with a title race with Arsenal still in full swing that could well have to wait until next season if he is still at the club.

Sports.title: How footie fans are fuming at ‘historic’ World Cup half time show featuring Madonna as they slam ‘Super Bowl knock-off’
Sports.content:
WORLD Cup chiefs recruited puppets from The Muppets and Sesame Street to launch the first ever half-time show planned for the tournament’s final.

Kermit, Miss Piggy, Animal and Elmo joined Coldplay frontman Chris Martin in a Fifa video unveiled yesterday to announce the star-studded line-up for the event.





The glitzy extravaganza, like those seen at the US Super Bowl, will ­feature Madonna, Shakira and K-pop boy band BTS.

In the video, singer Chris says it will be “a chance to show how ­amazing all different kinds of humans are”, as Elmo phones the A-listers to invite them to perform.

But the guest superstars may have to be quick with their acts as ­football’s current laws say the half-time break cannot exceed 15 minutes.

Sources say this could leave them with a window of just 11 minutes to pour out their hits in front of fans at the 82,500-seat MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

However, the regulation 15 minutes was extended at the 2024 Copa America final between Colombia and Argentina, where Shakira performed within a 25-minute break.

That move was blasted by Colombia coach Nestor Lorenzo at the time, who raged: “I think it should be like any other match, with the 15 minutes that ­correspond to the regulations.

“One knows the cost of those recovery minutes in the locker room. Players can cool down too much.”

He went on to point out that ­football authorities often penalise managers if their team returns to the pitch just a minute late.



But half-time shows are the norm at major US sporting events.

At last year’s Club World Cup final in the US between Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain, the interval also overran to 24 minutes.

Football purists have raised ­concerns that extending breaks beyond 15 minutes upsets the players’ rhythm and match-readiness.



But Fifa president Gianni Infantino has defended the move towards longer, glitzy shows, declaring the 2026 half-time entertainment will mark a “historic moment”.

He added: “We need the half-time show which is not just a show but which carries an important message . . . how we can impact the world by putting together the No1 sport in the world — which is soccer or football, call it as you want — and music.”

Queen of Pop Madonna, who is the best-selling female artist of all time, will top the bill at the July 19 final, which will be the climax of 104 matches being played in the US, Canada and Mexico.

The 67-year-old diva recently relaunched her career with a surprise appearance at the Coachella festival alongside Sabrina ­Carpenter for duets of her hits Vogue and Like A Prayer.

Madonna headlined the Super Bowl half-time show in 2012, while Shakira shared the stage with Jennifer Lopez at the event in 2020.



Shakira also sang the official song for the 2010 World Cup in South Africa. Called Waka Waka (This Time For Africa), it raises the possibility of a duet, this time with Muppet Fozzie Bear, whose comedy catchphrase is Wocka Wocka!

Meanwhile, she will be releasing this year’s official tournament song, Dai Dai.

Named after an Italian phrase meaning “come on”, the track also features Nigerian singer Burna Boy.



K-pop band BTS, the best-selling music act in South Korean history, have made a comeback after ­completing three years of compulsory military service.

The seven-member group had a UK No3 with My ­Universe ­alongside Coldplay in 2021. Infantino, who is also facing fan fury over the extortionate prices of World Cup tickets, said the show “will be a historic moment for the Fifa World Cup, befitting the biggest sporting event in the world”.

But fan groups do not agree.

The England Football Supporters’ Association hit out at the “spectacle-first” approach.

An association spokesman said real fans were being “priced out” in favour of “event-goers” who are there to enjoy music.



Football Supporters Europe also blasted what it calls the “juvenile daydreams of extended half-time shows and Super Bowl knock-offs”.

And even the biggest stars in the world will struggle to be worth the astonishing ticket prices being charged for the final.

Fifa has ramped up its top-tier pricing to £24,400, compared to £8,100 for the final between Argentina and France in Qatar in 2022.



And prices on the official resale platform — from which Fifa pockets a 30 per cent share of every ­transaction — have rocketed to incredible levels.

The current record being asked for a ticket on an official Fifa site is £8.5million for a ­single seat in Block 307, Row 22.

The half-time show is being staged in support of Fifa partner the Global Citizen Education Fund, which aims to raise $100million to help children worldwide.

In the launch video, Chris was seated with puppet Elmo to discuss how he wanted to create a ­performance to promote unity.

Muppets Cookie Monster, Animal, Kermit, Miss Piggy and Statler and Waldorf all had cameos to help reveal the big names set to ­perform. Anthony Alfano, Global Citizen’s director of artist engagement, said the plan was to raise awareness of global issues — as well as a huge sum for good causes.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Pop fans shared their excitement online yesterday as the line-up was revealed. One gushed: “It’s a dream come true to see Queen of Pop Madonna with our Latina Queen Shakira. Am I daydreaming?”

They could equally have been talking about the ticket prices.

Sports.title: Chelsea handed massive injury boost ahead of FA Cup final with stars set to return to key positions against Man City
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’S injury crisis has eased in time for the FA Cup final.

The Blues were without all five of their senior wingers at Liverpool last weekend, with Marc Cucurella deployed on the left.





However, ahead of Saturday’s final against Manchester City, Pedro Neto and Alejandro Garnacho have returned to training.

Interim boss Calum McFarlane is hopeful both can be involved at Wembley.

Reece James and Levi Colwill have also both recently returned from injury and have come through another week of training without issue.

McFarlane said: “Pedro Neto and Alex Garnacho have trained well this week, so looking really good, really hopeful with them. Positive signs.

“Happy with Reece. Good to get him some minutes before he played well when he came on as well. Largely positive around Reece.

“We were confident he was able to play those minutes in Liverpool. He came through them well. He’s trained well this week.”

Colwill suffered an ACL injury on day one of pre-season last summer and made his return from the bench against Nottingham Forest before starting at Anfield.

McFarlane added: “He has a really good rehab. He’d played a few games before. He played for us against Forest.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“His first game back was he played for the [Under] 21s two or three times. A really good training week for Levi.

“He was exceptional against Liverpool. So, again, we’re really hopeful. He played really well against Liverpool. He was exceptional.

“It speaks a lot about being able to put that sort of performance in after that time off at a really difficult place. He’s trained well this week and we’re looking forward to potentially having him on Saturday as well.”



Robert Sanchez is also fit once again but McFarlane would not reveal whether he or Filip Jorgensen would start against City.

He added: “I don’t think I’m going to reveal my starting line-up on two days before the game.

“Really positive, he’s trained well this week and we’re really hopeful to get him to Saturday.”

Sports.title: Golf superstar Justin Rose rocks up to PGA Championship in new Chelsea kit BEFORE it’s even been released
Sports.content:
GOLF icon Justin Rose arrived at the PGA Championship wearing the new Chelsea home shirt – before it has even been released.

The 45-year-old gave a nod to cameras on his way into Aronimink Golf Club while showing off the Blue kit.





The long-sleeved top had yellow detailing and the iconic Chelsea badge.

Rose, a boyhood Blues fan, shared a clip of his arrival on social media with a shirt emoji alongside the eyes emoji.

Fans were quick to comment, with one person writing: “Proper Chels, good luck this weekend!”

Another said: “Up the Chels. Best of luck this week Rosey.”

While a third joked: “Let’s hope you don’t perform as poor as them Rosey!”

A new image of the 2026-27 Chelsea home kit was ‘leaked’ on social media last week.

The strip in question looked similar to the one that Rose – who finished his first round tied in 34th on level par – was filmed wearing it on Thursday.

However, it features a faded club crest in the middle, which was not on the Brit’s new shirt.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Many Chelsea fans were not happy with the new design, with one person commenting: “This can’t be real, it’s disgusting.”

Ahead of the PGA Championship at the Aronimink Golf Club in Pennsylvania this week, Rose said: “I think after The Masters I went home and there was a lot to absorb there, that was a tough loss.

“I think, to be honest with you, the first two weeks back have been just about finding my feet again.

Sports.title: Man City beat Man Utd in FA Youth Cup final as ex-Premier League star's son nets winner
Sports.content:
Man City beat Man Utd in FA Youth Cup final as ex-Premier League star's son nets winner

MANCHESTER CITY 2-1 MANCHESTER UNITED: An 87th-minute goal from Reigan Heskey saw Manchester City win the FA Youth Cup for the fifth time in their history against bitter rivals United

View 2 Images The FA Youth Cup is back in Manchester City's hands (Image: Naomi Baker/Getty Images)

Manchester City have been crowned FA Youth Cup champions after beating rivals Manchester United 2-1 in dramatic fashion. Reigan Heskey, son of former Premier League striker Emile, scored a stunning goal in the 87th minute to put blue ribbons on the trophy.

‌



City had taken the lead in style, too, as Floyd Samba converted a free-kick from 25 yards in the first half. United hit back two minutes later through Godwill Kukonki, who drove forward from centre-back to finish off a brilliant move.

‌



But Darren Fletcher's youngsters were left heartbroken when Heskey, 18, found space on the left-hand side of the penalty area and chopped inside. The winger produced a thumping right-footed strike to ultimately win the game for Oliver Reiss' side.

‌



There were a host of recognisable faces in the stands of the 7,000-capacity Joie Stadium, which was controversially chosen as the venue for Thursday's final after the Etihad Stadium was made unavailable due to ongoing construction work. First-team managers Pep Guardiola and Michael Carrick watched on as the stars of the future battled it out.

Sports.title: Middlesbrough Spygate appeal truth explained as Southampton set for hearing
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough Spygate appeal truth explained as Southampton set for hearing

Middlesbrough fell to defeat against Southampton in the play-off semi-final, but are still awaiting the outcome of an EFL charge against the Saints.

View 2 Images Southampton booked their place in the Championship play-off final with a 2-1 extra-time win over Middlesbrough. (Image: Robin Jones, Getty Images)

Middlesbrough won't be allowed to launch an appeal against any verdict reached by an independent commission regarding a charge brought against Southampton over spying allegations. Spygate has dominated the headlines in recent days after Boro suffered defeat to the Saints in the Championship play-offs.

‌



In the build-up to the first leg at the Riverside at the weekend, Middlesbrough caught a member of Southampton's analysis team reportedly spying on their preparations for the match.

‌



Observing an opposing team's training sessions in the days preceding a fixture is a violation of EFL regulations. The rule was introduced after a similar incident between Leeds United and Derby County back in 2019.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Southampton have subsequently been charged with breaching the rules, with the EFL confirming that the hearing will take place on or before Tuesday, 19 May, just four days before the play-off final.

One possible outcome, should Southampton be found guilty, is that they are thrown out of the play-offs, with Boro taking their place in the final at Wembley.

‌



In preparation for that scenario, the Middlesbrough squad will keep training this week, with the play-off final scheduled for Saturday, 23 May.

Sky broadcasts more than 1,400 live matches across the Premier League, EFL and more with at least 215 live from the top flight alongside Formula 1, darts and golf.

Southampton are currently scheduled to face Hull City in the showpiece match. The Tigers beat Millwall 2-0 in their semi-final to book their place at Wembley.

‌



Should the verdict fail to go the way Middlesbrough hope, the club will have no power to contest the outcome. This is because Boro will play no part in the hearing, despite having originally lodged the complaint with the EFL.

Instead, the proceedings will be conducted solely between the EFL as the prosecuting party and Southampton as the defendant. It will therefore fall to either the EFL or Southampton to pursue any appeal against the final ruling.

View 2 Images Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg issued an emotional response to the situation (Image: Warren Little, Getty Images)

‌



Nevertheless, Boro could potentially pursue separate legal action against either the EFL or Southampton once the case has concluded. It would likely be seeking compensation.

Manager Kim Hellberg delivered an emotional response when addressing the situation immediately after the play-off semi-final defeat. "I'm just disappointed," he said.

"I'm just sad that it can work that way, that you break those types of rules.

"It just makes me sad. But there's a lot of love and there's a lot of things that are very, very beautiful about football."

Sports.content:
'Evil' - Hull City owner breaks silence on Spygate as play-off final hangs in balance

The Championship play-off final between Hull City and Southampton could be postponed after the Saints were charged by the EFL over allegedly spying on their semi-final opponents, Middlesbrough

View 3 Images Acun Ilcal has given his verdict on Spygate (Image: Beyza Comert/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Hull City owner Acun Ilicali has accused those responsible for Spygate of putting 'evil' into the football world. The Tigers are currently due face Southampton in the Championship play-off final at Wembley next Saturday, but the richest game in football is at risk of being postponed.

‌



The Saints have been charged by the EFL after it emerged that one of their analysts had spied on Middlesbrough's training session ahead of their semi-final first leg. Southampton could be kicked out of the play-offs as a result, although an appeal process may force the final to be pushed back to a later date.

‌



While Middlesbrough's players and staff have delayed their summer holidays and will return to training on Monday, Hull chief Ilicali has given his verdict. "I don't know what the officials will decide," Ilicali told talkSPORT.

‌



"I don't want to make any statements because it's something that is being investigated. We don't know who is involved or who is responsible. At this time, it's better for me not to comment."

Asked how he'd feel if someone spied on Hull, the Turkish owner replied: "I would be furious. If everything is completely true and there is zero doubt, I would be furious.

‌



"And I would ask this question: How many times has it happened before. I would be very, very angry, of course, if everything is so solid. As a person, I don't understand why people do things like that.

"I always run for justice in my life. But you see many things in life that surprises you, and on this I am surprised too. I know the owners of Southampton - they are good people and I am sure this is nothing to do with them.

"But whoever is involved on the technical side, I do not know. Whoever is involved, I think, put evil in the football world this week."

‌



Should Southampton be kicked out of the play-offs? Have your say in the comments section.

On whether Southampton should face explosion from the play-offs, Ilicali admitted: "I'm not sure. For example, what happens in a game if someone dives to help their side win a trophy? In football, there are sometimes these kind of things.

‌



"The punishment, what it should be, it's hard to know without a clear mind. But in football, you can dive to win a penalty and get a penalty. Or hand of god, for example, some cheating happen in football sometimes.

"Whether they should be punished, and how they should be punished, it's hard for me to comment because, at the end of the day, they will probably be our opponent and I don't want to speak negatively about our opponent."

View 3 Images Acun Ilcal tried to remain diplomatic (Image: Freddie Yeo/MB Media/Getty Images)

‌



Although their opponents in the final could change, Hull know that they'll eventually go to Wembley and vie for a spot in the Premier League, having dramatically made the play-offs on the final day. "It's one game - a big game for us," Ilicali, who purchased the club in 2022, added.

"If we win, we're going to be in the Premier League, and that's our dream. When you see our team, you see a very united team, everyone is dying for this game and the fans are very hungry.

"These games are 50-50 games and crucial moments will decide. I think whether it's Southampton or Middlesbrough, it's 50-50 and we have every chance.

Sports.title: Nicky Butt unleashes on Spygate drama and claims manager 'should be SACKED on the spot'
Sports.content:
Nicky Butt unleashes on Spygate drama and claims manager 'should be SACKED on the spot'

Nicky Butt has given his take after Southampton were charged last week by the EFL with spying on a training session held by Middlesbrough before their play-off semi-final

View 2 Images Nicky Butt (Image: (Justin Setterfield/Getty Images))

Nicky Butt believes Southampton boss Tonda Eckert should be sacked if he and his scouting team need to 'spy' on Middlesbrough this late in the season. The Saints face an anxious wait to learn whether the 'Spygate' scandal will cost them a place in the Championship play-off final.

‌



Eckert’s side completed a 2-1 aggregate victory over Middlesbrough in the semi-final on Tuesday night to set up a Wembley meeting with Hull on May 23. However, they now face an independent commission hearing after being charged by the EFL for allegedly spying on a Boro training session last week.

‌



The EFL issued a statement on Thursday afternoon to say the hearing would take place “on or before Tuesday, May 19”. But the game at Wembley a week on Saturday appears to be in doubt, given an appeal from one or more parties in the case seems almost certain.

‌



However, offering his take, Butt didn’t hold back, and after claiming that if Southampton needed to watch a Middlesbrough training session after a full season, then Eckert and his club’s recruitment and scouting team should be sacked on the spot, he also took aim at Kim Hellberg for the way he has reacted.

"It's been going on for years,” he said via Paddy Power. “I remember when we first started playing in Europe, I was probably about 20, we used to always train the night before a game at the ground and the manager would never ever, ever do the real starting eleven.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Spygate hearing date set as Southampton face expulsion and play-off final at risk READ MORE :

EFL release statement on Spygate as Championship play-off final could be POSTPONED READ MORE :

"He'd always do a fake one. He'd never do set pieces, he'd have two star players limp off with ice packs on their hamstring because he was always thinking people were watching.

"People can say, ‘It's not right, it's cheating’. It's just what it is in high level football. Teams will know the starting eleven, you know all the players, you can just go and watch games anytime you want. They can see it all on WyScout.

"It's a bit stupid really. If Southampton need to watch Middlesbrough like this after a full season then the manager and all the recruitment team and all the scouting team should be sacked on the spot.

‌



"They should know everything about them - there's no secrets in football. They know who's injured, they know who's not injured.

View 2 Images Tonda Eckert's side are waiting to discover their fate (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

"Anyone who is 80 per cent fit to play will play in a semi-final second leg. It is a ruling in the FA, and I get it, but it's been going on for years and it will go on for years again.

‌



"I don't see the problem with it. You can go and watch training at most grounds from a distance.

"Maybe some of the high level Premier League ones are like Fort Knox, but most grounds up and down the country and around the world you can get within 100 metres of a fence to watch training.

"What are you going to be able to tell the manager the next day? ‘I know how to beat Middlesbrough because I've seen a lad do a little run down the side’. It's just bulls***, it's ridiculous. It’s so childish. It will happen with every single manager.

Article continues below

"But any manager that calls people cheats over it are hypocrites because they're doing exactly the same. Maybe not through their own eyes but through sending other people to watch it."

Sports.title: 'Embarrassing' - Unai Emery fires Liverpool clear message over Harvey Elliott loan saga
Sports.content:
'Embarrassing' - Unai Emery fires Liverpool clear message over Harvey Elliott loan saga

Harvey Elliott is nearing the end of his frustrating season on loan at Aston Villa, where he has barely featured due to a clause in the agreement with Liverpool

View 2 Images Harvey Elliott has barely played for Aston Villa during his loan spell (Image: Nigel French/Getty Images)

Unai Emery has admitted that Harvey Elliott's wasted season on loan at Aston Villa is "embarrassing for everyone involved". Elliott has barely featured during his loan spell from Liverpool due to a clause in the agreement between the two clubs.

‌



The 23-year-old midfielder moved to Villa Park in search of more regular game time, yet has only made nine appearances across all competitions for Villa this season. He has made four of those appearances in the Premier League, totalling just 109 minutes of action.

‌



That is due to the fact that Villa would have to sign him permanently from Liverpool for £35million if he reached 10 league appearances. Back in February, Villa manager Emery accused Liverpool of "damaging" Elliott with the terms of the loan agreement.

‌



Speaking ahead of their Premier League game against Liverpool on Friday night, Emery has now apologised to Elliott and spread the blame out. “It is something embarrassing for everyone involved in it. My apologies for Harvey Elliott are every day in my mind," he said.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Anthony Gordon sent brutal Bayern Munich warning as Liverpool and Arsenal lurk READ MORE :

Liverpool injury news and return dates as Florian Wirtz and Mohamed Salah updates given READ MORE :

“But it is the responsibility. We have our responsibility and Liverpool have their responsibility. As a human and as a person, how the season has gone has been difficult.”

‌



Liverpool manager Arne Slot also addressed the subject in his pre-match press conference, in which he confirmed Elliott will return to the club over the summer for pre-season.

"I think for him, for everyone, it didn’t work out as he wanted it, as we wanted it and probably also how Villa wanted it, because you usually sign a player or bring him in on loan to use him," Slot said.

“That hasn’t happened a lot. That’s not for me to answer why that is. But of course, it’s never nice for a player not to make so many minutes, especially after the season he had with us, where he made – I assume – even more minutes with us than these 280.

‌



View 2 Images Unai Emery has spoken openly about Harvey Elliott's situation (Image: Getty Images)

“He went over there to get more playing time, but unfortunately that didn’t happen. And for such a talented player that did so well in the U21 Euros [last summer], you want a player like that to get more and more playing time.

“He went to a very, very good team as well, where they also have a lot of good players. I don’t know why he hasn’t made the minutes he was expecting. That’s not for me to answer.

‌



“But it’s always a pity if a player hardly plays for two years, let alone a player of that age that has shown during the [U21] Euros that he’s such a good player.”

Liverpool refused to recall Elliott in the January transfer window and it seems unlikely that they will change their mind over his future. The England under-21 star's Liverpool contract runs until June 2027, but a summer transfer appears on the cards once his Villa purgatory has ended.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson's stance on Michael Carrick becoming new Man Utd boss emerges after agreement
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson's stance on Michael Carrick becoming new Man Utd boss emerges after agreement

Sir Alex Ferguson has a different role when it comes to Manchester United managerial appointments

View 3 Images Alex Ferguson has made his thoughts clear on Michael Carrick (Image: John Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images.)

Sir Alex Ferguson has endorsed Michael Carrick's expected appointment as the permanent Manchester United manager. United have explored other options but Carrick has long been considered the front-runner.

‌



Crucially, co-owners the Glazer and Sir Jim Ratcliffe are in agreement that he deserves to stay in the post. That backing extends to the club's greatest ever manager, Ferguson.

‌



After retiring in 2013, the Scot was regularly consulted on managerial decisions. While that hasn't been the case on this occasion, it is understood he backs the likely permanent appointment of Carrick, as we reported yesterday. Carrick would be the seventh permanent boss since Ferguson stood down.

‌



Ferguson hand-picked his successor, David Moyes, but has had less involvement in recent years. He was in favour of Jose Mourinho's appointment in 2026, jokingly telling the Portuguese coach to "bring an umbrella" for Manchester's inclement weather.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mourinho said of Ferguson at the time: "His opinion is an important opinion for me in the same way that many legends in this club love the club and are in the punditry industry, so every opinion will be important for me."

‌



Ex-Sir Alex Ferguson assistant warns Man Utd have already made Michael Carrick error READ MORE :

Ex-Man Utd star demands the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe sell up in brutal rant READ MORE :

Ferguson also appeared to get on well with Erik ten Hag, going out for dinner with the Dutch coach. While Ferguson, a non-executive director, hasn't been directly consulted recently, he has been kept abreast of developments regarding Carrick.

The ex-Middlesbrough boss has surpassed expectations since taking over in January following an acrimonious end to Ruben Amorim's rocky reign.

Carrick has overseen a marked improvement in mood and results, with United clinching Champions League qualification with three matches to spare and on the verge of securing third spot in the Premier League.

‌



View 3 Images Carrick looks set to be appointed permanently (Image: Getty Images)

That upturn has put the club's former midfielder, captain and coach in pole position to stay in the post, with talking place before the end of the season.

Carrick also has support from some of his former United team-mates, including Wayne Rooney and Rio Ferdinand. Rooney has told the club to make a final decision sooner rather than later, ahead of what should be a busy summer of arrivals and departures as Carrick reshapes the squad.

‌



View 3 Images Ferguson isn't directly consulted on managerial appointments anymore (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Speaking on Match of the Day, Rooney said: "I think for the club to announce him, I think they need to do it swiftly because they need to get players in. They need to get players to improve that team."

Meanwhile, Ferdinand told talkSPORT: "He's earned the right to manage Manchester United. He's taken us to third convincingly. On that alone, he deserves an opportunity."

Sports.title: EFL release statement on Spygate as Championship play-off final could be POSTPONED
Sports.content:
EFL release statement on Spygate as Championship play-off final could be POSTPONED

Southampton's place in the Championship play-off final against Hull City remains up in the air, with the EFL confirming the plan for their disciplinary panel into spying allegations

View 3 Images The Championship playoff final is scheduled for May 23 (Image: Getty Images)

The EFL have confirmed that the Championship play-off final could still be postponed due to the hearing into the Southampton spying allegations. Saints are accused of spying on Middlesbrough training before their semi-final first leg and their place in the final against Hull City remains uncertain.

‌



As Mirror Football exclusively revealed on Thursday, a commission made up of three legal experts is expected to hold the meeting behind closed doors in London to decide Southampton's fate. The EFL now says their decision will be made by Tuesday, hopefully allowing enough time for the matter to be settled before the final on Saturday, May 23, with a kick-off time of 4.30pm.

‌



It is alleged that a member of Southampton's staff was caught filming Boro's training session two days before the first leg, which finished 0-0.

‌



The EFL said in a statement: "The EFL can today provide an interim update on the ongoing disciplinary proceedings involving Southampton following Tuesday’s Championship Play-Off Semi-Final Second Leg.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

SpyGate hearing date set as Southampton face expulsion and play-off final at risk READ MORE :

"The Independent Disciplinary Commission hearing will take place on or before Tuesday, 19 May. The exact date remains under discussion and is expected to be confirmed shortly.

‌



"The Commission will issue its decision as soon as possible following consideration of the relevant submissions and evidence. As the proceedings are being conducted by an Independent Disciplinary Commission, the EFL does not control the proposed timetable.

"Notwithstanding this, the EFL continues to plan on the basis that the Championship Play-Off Final will take place as scheduled on Saturday 23 May, with the kick-off time confirmed as 4.30pm. Supporters should, however, be aware that the outcome of the disciplinary proceedings may yet result in changes to the fixture.

View 3 Images Tonda Eckert's side are waiting to discover their fate (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

‌



"The EFL has a number of contingency plans should they be required, which also includes consideration of any appeal process, if required."

The hearing into the Southampton allegations has created a nightmare scenario for supporters planning to go to the play-off final. Both Hull and Saints have delayed releasing ticket information due to the uncertainty, with just nine days until the fixture.

The EFL added: "Hull City and Southampton will share further information on their respective sales processes later today.

‌



"Sales will be subject to usual terms and conditions, and in the circumstances, fans are encouraged to pay particular attention to the terms and conditions.

View 3 Images Southampton beat Middlesbrough 2-1 on aggregate to reach the final (Image: Warren Little, Getty Images)

"Likewise, supporters should consider the situation when booking any associated travel and accommodation. This decision follows ongoing coordination with the Clubs to ensure that on-sale arrangements can be implemented as soon as practicable.

‌



"The League recognises that this complex situation has caused concern and disruption for supporters, particularly those making travel arrangements, and will continue to provide as much clarity as possible.

"However, in these clearly exceptional circumstances, the League considers this to be the most appropriate course of action."

Sports.title: Humphries surges to first Premier League nightly win to reach Play-Offs
Sports.content:
Luke Humphries surged to his first Premier League nightly success with wins against Luke Littler and Gerwyn Price in Birmingham to reach Finals Night at London's O2.

Humphries kicked off the night with a whitewash win over Stephen Bunting, before defeating world No 1 Luke Littler and then Gerwyn Price in the final.

He took out 117, and averaged 100.16 for 6-4 glory against Price meaning all four of the Play-Off spots have now been confirmed.

Luke Humphries 6-4 Gerwyn Price

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Humphries said he was 'incredibly proud' after sealing the final Play-Off spot

"I'm incredibly proud of myself, probably the most proud I've ever been in my life. For me, the last two Premier Leagues have been easy, getting through in 14 weeks," said former world champion, Humphries.

"For the last few weeks there has been a lot of pressure on my shoulders. To make three finals and win one means a lot. I get written off a lot as a player but this means I have that grit and determination."

He added: "Yes [there was a point where I thought I wouldn't make Finals Night]. When you are five points outside the top four you think you need a miracle.

"But in the back of my mind and my girlfriend's mind, we knew I had it in me. I needed someone to tell me I could do it, and I've believed in myself that last few weeks.

"I'm really proud because it would have hurt me had I not defended the title at The O2."

🚨 Luke Humphries qualifies for the Play-Offs!

He finally picks up his first weekly title of the year, as the reigning Champion returns to the O2 with a week to spare.

Sports.title: St Helens hold off Huddersfield to go top of Super League
Sports.content:
St Helens moved to the top of the Super League after fending off Huddersfield Giants to earn a 18-16 victory on Thursday.

Paul Rowley's side bounced back from a heavy 32-0 defeat to rivals Wigan Warriors in the Challenge Cup semi-finals by making it five consecutive wins in the league and will keep a close eye on second-placed Leeds Rhinos, who can return to top spot if they beat Wigan Warriors on Friday, live on Sky Sports.

Four first-half tries from Harry Robertson, Lewis Murphy, Owen Dagnall and George Delaney put St Helens 24-0 up at half-time in Huddersfield but the home side came back in the second half.

Tries from Asher O'Donnell, Adam Swift and Niall Evalds gave St Helens a minor scare but Huddersfield were left with too much to do and lost their ninth game of the Super League season to remain bottom of the table.

"We allowed for chaos with some of the stuff we dished out but the stop-start nature [of the match], then you lose concentration, it became unattractive to watch and play in," Rowley told Sky Sports.

"So it was an ugly second half but credit to Huddersfield for fighting back and showing some heart to get back in it and get us nervous at the end."

Image: Huddersfield Giants attempted a comeback from 24-0 down at half time but were unable to really get back into the match (SW Pix)

It was the last match in charge for interim Huddersfield coach Liam Finn before Australian Jim Lenihan arrives in the UK next week.

Finn took over from Luke Robinson in March after Huddersfield lost their opening five league games, and won his first two matches as interim coach. But, Huddersfield have now lost four league games in a row and face a relegation battle this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Huddersfield Giants interim head coach Liam Finn says he will be part of the future coaching setup under Jim Lenihan

How St Helens fended off Huddersfield

An early break from Jack Welsby helped Harry Robertson touch down for the Saints, with Lewis Murphy then punishing poor handling from Huddersfield to go over in the corner.

Winger Dagnall added a third try for Saints in the 18th minute before George Delaney capitalised on another Huddersfield mistake just before half-time.

Huddersfield rallied after the restart, with O'Donnell taking down a loose ball from Tui Lolohea's kick. Further tries from Swift, against his former club, and Giants full-back Evalds, with six minutes left, looked to set up a tense finish.

However, Jackson Hastings had crucially landed a penalty in the 65th minute, which proved enough to see Saints home.

Image: Jackson Hastings' second-half penalty for St Helens relieved some of the pressure from Huddersfield (SW Pix)

Sports.title: 'I'm massively fired up' - Whitlock explains retirement U-turn as he targets LA 2028
Sports.content:
Max Whitlock explained to Sky Sports News why he's returned to gymnastics

Three-time Olympic champion Max Whitlock says he's "massively fired up" and did not need to persuade his family to come out of retirement.

Whitlock retired from gymnastics following the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris but made a shock return at the end of last year and is hoping to earn a place in the Team GB squad for Los Angeles 2028.

The Briton will be 35 years old at the next Olympics in LA and says he wants to take his main disciple, the pommel horse, "further than I've ever pushed it".

"It's incredible to be back. It feels amazing to be able to say that I'm a gymnast again, I'm an athlete," he told Sky Sports News.

"I've just competed my first international back. Some good bits, some but not so good bits, but loads to work on, so I'm massively fired up.

"We're gearing up towards Commonwealth Games and World Championships, so I'm back in the thick of it, and it's very exciting. We've got just over two years to LA, that's my end goal. And trust me, I will be done after LA, I will be finished!"

Whitlock was "itching" to make a U-turn on his retirement decision after failing to win a medal in Paris 2024

Whitlock: I didn't want any regrets

Whitlock burst onto the scene at London 2012 with bronze medals in the team and pommel horse events, before winning two golds in Rio 2016 on the floor and pommel horse.

He defended his pommel horse title at Tokyo 2020 and was a strong medal hopeful for Paris 2024, but finished fourth and failed to come away with a medal.

The 33-year-old admits missing out on a medal was "a lot tougher" than he expected and that his career "didn't finish in the right way".

The 33-year-old won two golds at Rio 2016

"I couldn't fight the feeling that something was just constantly itching out of me and just almost thinking 'there's more I could do'," said Whitlock.

"Then I feel like, fast forward 20 years time, would I regret not coming back for two years and that final push to really squeeze everything I possibly can at sport?

"I still feel like my body can give more. I still feel like in my head I can do more physically, mentally. I want to prove that to myself and do everything I can."

Whitlock is building up to the Commonwealth Games and World Championships later this year

He added: "I think that I'm very lucky to be in this position. There was zero persuasion. I think a lot of people, the people real close to me, saw that something was missing. Me saying, 'actually I'm coming back', saying that to my family, making a decision with them not only brings smiles to their faces.

"My wife is mega excited for me to be back. [My daughter] Willow is mega, mega excited for me and my whole family, my mum, dad, my brother, everyone's excited about it come out to the competitions again and watch me compete.

"I think they really kind of felt a bit of a gap when I said that I'm done."

Sports.title: Bolton hit Bradford with sucker-punch to reach L1 play-off final
Sports.content:
Bolton reached the Sky Bet League One play-off final after clinching 1-0 semi-final second leg win at Bradford. Xavier Simons scored the only goal to seal a 2-0 aggregate victory.

For the most part, it was a cagey and fraught encounter at Valley Parade where chances came at a premium. It was 68 minutes until the first shot on target.

They decisive period of the game came in a period of 68 second-half seconds.

Image: Bolton players celebrate Xavier Simons' late goal that sealed a 2-0 aggregate win over Bradford

Bantams forward Kayden Jackson was adjudged to have been offside when he headed in, and from the counter-attack that followed, Xavier Simons slammed home to take the game out of their reach.

Steven Schumacher's side will face Stockport at Wembley on Sunday May 24, with a place in the Sky Bet Championship on the line.
